title: Audit Ingest Collector Designs and Evidence Workflow Notes
content:
Purpose:
This doc captures engineering notes for designing the audit-event ingest collectors and the control-evidence workflow that ties into RBAC v2 decisions and SIEM exports. Aim is to define a practical, testable collector behavior that:
- reliably attaches RBAC context to audit events,
- keeps evidence manifests tamper-evident, and
- supports serum-style SIEM exports (JSON + CEF fallback) while preserving low-latency for hosted API paths.

Scope and non-goals:
- In-scope: event schema v2 field set, collector buffering/backpressure, dedup/ordering, evidence manifest format, enrichment with RBAC v2 snapshots, export adapters for Splunk/Datadog/QRadar.
- Out-of-scope: deep dive into private-deploy packaging (handled separately), long-term cold-storage archival (handled by compliance infra).

High-level flow (notes):
1) Source emits raw audit event (model-infer:start, model-load, api-key:create, role:update) with minimal fields (timestamp, actor_id, request_id, action, resource_id).
2) Collector receives event and immediately attaches ingest metadata (collector_id, ingest_ts, sha256_of_payload).
3) Collector queries RBAC v2 snapshot service for actor_id -> effective role(s) at event timestamp. Collector caches snapshots for 2 minutes with jittered TTL.
4) Collector emits enriched audit record to primary internal audit topic (kafka/partitioned by org_id) and writes an evidence manifest record to the evidence index (for compliance queries).
5) SIEM export adapter consumes primary topic and sends required fields to external SIEMs, respecting PII minimization rules.

Audit log schema v2 (required fields):
- schema_version: string ("audit_v2")
- event_id: string (uuid v4)
- timestamp: ISO8601 string (UTC)
- actor_id: string (user:<id> | service:<id>)
- request_id: string (api request correlation)
- action: string (e.g., "model.generate", "api.key.create")
- resource_type: string (model|deployment|api_key|secret|role)
- resource_id: string
- rbac_snapshot_id: string (id referencing RBAC snapshot used to enrich)
- rbac_effective_roles: string[] (list of role ids as strings)
- decision_context: string (short text summarizing why a decision was made; not a policy dump)
- outcome: string (allowed|denied|warn|observed)
- metadata: string (flat JSON-stringified map for free-form structured bits; keep small)
- collector_id: string
- ingest_ts: ISO8601 string
- payload_checksum: string (sha256 hex)
- evidence_ref: string (evidence manifest id)

Notes on schema choices:
- metadata is a string to avoid heavy, nested structures in the main index; parsing downstream should consider size limits.
- rbac_effective_roles intentionally duplicates the main decision data so SIEMs can filter without RBAC lookups.

Evidence manifest format (design w/ fields we need for controls mapping):
- manifest_id (uuid)
- related_event_ids (list of event_id)
- control_ids (list of control identifiers, e.g., CTRL-AUD-001)
- evidence_type (string: log|screenshot|config-dump|policy-snapshot)
- resource_snapshot_pointer (opaque pointer to archived object, e.g., s3://evidence/...)
- signer (service id that produced manifest)
- signature (detached signature base64 over manifest payload)
- retention_ttl_days (integer as string)
- created_at (ISO)

Operational guarantees we aim for:
- At-least-once delivery to primary audit topic.
- Idempotent evidence manifest writes using manifest_id and event_id dedup index.
- Dedup key for events: sha256(event.payload || event.request_id || actor_id).
- Ordering: best-effort per request_id. No strict global ordering requirement.

Collector behavior and components (implementation notes):
- Ingest endpoint: accepts batch or single JSON lines, validates schema minimally, responds with 202 + provisional ids.
- Local buffer: bounded in-memory ring buffer (size configurable) + persistent spool to disk when memory pressure high. Spool files rotated hourly with checksum footers.
- RBAC fetch strategy: 
  - Primary: call snapshot-service for exact timestamp match.
  - Fallback: use most-recent snapshot if timestamp outside retention window and mark rbac_snapshot_id = "stale".
  - Cache invalidation: event-driven when RBAC changes (webhook) marks cache entries for org invalidation.
- Enrichment pipeline: validation -> rbac enrichment -> checksum -> write-to-topic -> evidence-index write. Each stage annotated with an internal trace id.

Integrity and tamper-evidence:
- All collectors append payload_checksum and sign manifests with service key (KMS usage).
- Evidence index stores signer, signature, and raw payload pointer; an automated verifier job (daily) replays random samples and validates signatures.

SIEM export considerations:
- Exports should be configurable per-tenant: include/exclude fields to meet data residency and PII requirements.
- Two export modes: streaming (low-latency) and batched (hourly bulk for high-volume orgs).
- Support formats: JSON-Lines (default), CEF (for legacy), and vendor-specific EDMs.
- Throttling: per-tenant rate limiting for external SIEM endpoints. Retries with exponential backoff and dead-letter queue for unsent payloads.

RBAC v2 interactions (special cases):
- role-update events: if the actor changes permissions mid-request, we should record the RBAC snapshot pre-change and post-change if both happen within a 10s window. This produces two audit records linked to the same request_id.
- temporary elevations: collectors must attach a transient flag when the decision was influenced by a time-limited elevation (so downstream control checks can surface review items).

Backfill, replay, and stateful reprocessing:
- Backfill should accept a start/end timestamp and read archival logs. For each backfilled event we must tag it with backfill_job_id and do not overwrite original ingest_ts (keep original-author timestamps).
- Reprocessing rules: allow re-enrichment with newer RBAC snapshots but keep original rbac_snapshot_id as historical; create new derived_event with derived_event_id linking back to original_event_id.

Testing and validation plan (engineer checklist):
- Unit tests: checksum generation, dedup logic, schema sanitizer.
- Integration tests: collector -> topic -> evidence-index -> SIEM-adapter using testbed splunk emulator.
- Fuzz tests: random surplus fields in metadata to ensure truncation/sanitization.
- Failure injection: simulate RBAC API latency and assert collector falls back to cached snapshot and records a metric.
- Signed manifest verification job: test with rotated keys and ensure failures produce alerts.

Rollout phases (proposal):
- Alpha (internal): collectors deployed to dev cluster, SIEM adapter off, evidence-index in dev.
- Beta (select tenants): enable streaming exports for 3 pilot orgs, collect performance data, SLOs: 99th percentile enrich latency < 200ms for non-batched events.
- GA: export adapters hardened, docs updated, allow per-tenant export configs.

Operational metrics to surface in Console (high priority):
- ingest_rate (events/s),
- enrich_latency_p50/p95/p99,
- spool_disk_utilization,
- evidence_write_success_rate,
- siem_export_failure_rate,
- rbac_snapshot_miss_rate (how often collector had to fallback).

Open questions / TODOs:
- How granular should rbac_snapshot retention be? (30 days default?) Need compliance input.
- Do we want to include a compact delta of the effective role set rather than full list to reduce payload size? Trade-off: loses clarity for SIEM filtering.
- Define the exact signing key rotation cadence and KMS policy for collectors.
- Determine per-tenant PII redaction policies for SIEM exports (masking vs drop).

References and related docs:
- Confluence: Audit Schema v2 (linked above)
- Existing runbook: control-evidence-collector-runbook (see shared drive)
- SIEM export spec: evidence-automation-playbook-and-siem-export-spec (see shared drive)

Notes to reviewers:
- This is a working design doc. I'm leaning toward using a single "evidence manifest" per request_id where possible to reduce lookup cost; but we may need many manifests for long-running async jobs. Comments on tradeoffs welcome.
- If you touch the RBAC snapshot format, please add a compact serialized fingerprint field to avoid transferring large blobs into the audit index.
